items.title: Flavio Bolsonaro’s ‘corrupto’ stunt sparks viral meme before Brazil election runoff

sentences.en: Far-right presidential candidate’s TV debate swipe at rival backfires as people take to social media to parody it To Flávio Bolsonaro and his publicists, it must have seemed an ingenious idea that would expose his rival’s supposed crookedness on the eve of Brazil’s presidential election.
sentences.zh: 随着人们在社交媒体上模仿，极右翼总统候选人的电视辩论在竞争对手的反弹中大放异彩。对于弗拉维奥·博尔索纳罗（ Flávio Bolsonaro ）和他的公关人员来说，这似乎是一个巧妙的想法，将在巴西总统大选前夕揭露他的竞争对手的所谓歪曲。

sentences.en: But the far-right politician’s decision to attend a primetime television debate against his leftwing opponent, Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva, with the word “corrupto” (corrupt) written on the palm of his hand has backfired.
sentences.zh: 但是，这位极右翼政客决定参加针对左翼对手路易斯·伊纳西奥·卢拉·达席尔瓦（ Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva ）的黄金时段电视辩论，手掌上写着“腐败” （ corrupto ）一词，却适得其反。

items.title: Can a local git remote replace GitHub in your agent eval?

sentences.en: Can a local git remote replace GitHub in your agent eval?.
sentences.zh: 本地git远程是否可以替换代理eval中的GitHub ？。

sentences.en: When an agent eval involves pushing, pulling or keeping a git branch in sync, the fixture needs a remote repository.
sentences.zh: 当代理评估涉及推送、拉动或保持git分支同步时，夹具需要一个远程存储库。

sentences.en: The easiest one to set up is a bare repository next to the fixture.
sentences.zh: 最容易设置的是夹具旁边的裸存储库。

sentences.en: It takes one git init --bare , works offline and resets with the rest of the workspace.
sentences.zh: 它需要一个git init --bare ，离线工作，并与其他工作区一起重置。

sentences.en: A real GitHub repository in comparison, needs a token, an API call to create it and cleanup after every run.
sentences.zh: 相比之下，真正的GitHub存储库需要一个令牌，一个API调用来创建它，并在每次运行后进行清理。

sentences.en: Run scenarios in parallel, and it gets even worse.
sentences.zh: 并行运行场景，情况变得更糟。

sentences.en: Every run needs its own repository with a unique name that still looks like something a developer would create, and every failed teardown leaves one behind.
sentences.zh: 每次运行都需要自己的存储库，具有独特的名称，看起来仍然像开发人员会创建的东西，每次失败的拆卸都会留下一个。

sentences.en: Multiply that by hundreds of runs, and you’re also putting load on GitHub’s services for traffic that serves nobody.
sentences.zh: 乘以数百次运行，您还会为GitHub的服务加载不为任何人服务的流量。

sentences.en: So we wanted to know whether a local remote is a good enough stand-in for the real thing.
sentences.zh: 因此，我们想知道本地遥控器是否足以代替真实的遥控器。

sentences.en: Mostly, it is.
sentences.zh: 大多数情况下，确实如此。

sentences.en: The agent rebased just as well and pushed just as safely against both.
sentences.zh: 特工也重新设定了基地，并安全地对抗两者。

sentences.en: But when the agent had to decide on its own whether to push, the local remote changed the answer.
sentences.zh: 但是，当代理不得不自己决定是否推送时，本地远程更改了答案。

items.title: Introducing tsrs: A port of TypeScript to Rust

sentences.en: Introducing tsrs: A port of TypeScript to Rust.
sentences.zh: 引入tsrs ：将TypeScript移植到Rust。

sentences.en: Cloudflare and VoidZero are now working with Max Schwenk of Owner.com on tsrs , a Rust port of the TypeScript compiler.
sentences.zh: Cloudflare和VoidZero现在正在与Owner.com的Max Schwenk在tsrs上合作， tsrs是TypeScript编译器的Rust端口。

sentences.en: We are doing this work in close collaboration with the TypeScript team, and incubating tsrs as part of the Oxc JavaScript compiler toolchain .
sentences.zh: 我们正在与TypeScript团队密切合作开展这项工作，并将tsrs作为Oxc JavaScript编译器工具链的一部分进行孵化。

sentences.en: Our goal is to help developers spend less time waiting for their code to be checked and more time building.
sentences.zh: 我们的目标是帮助开发人员花更少的时间等待代码检查，花更多的时间构建代码。

sentences.en: Making TypeScript faster and more memory-efficient also helps bring complete development environments to more places, including right in your browser.
sentences.zh: 使TypeScript更快、更节省内存也有助于将完整的开发环境带到更多地方，包括浏览器中的位置。

sentences.en: To be clear, we are not forking TypeScript.
sentences.zh: 需要明确的是，我们不是在分叉TypeScript。

sentences.en: We believe the TypeScript team should remain in full control of the language’s design and direction.
sentences.zh: 我们认为TypeScript团队应该继续完全控制语言的设计和方向。

sentences.en: They have maintained a long-term vision while guiding TypeScript’s adoption across the JavaScript community.
sentences.zh: 他们一直保持着长期的愿景，同时指导TypeScript在JavaScript社区中的采用。

sentences.en: We do not want to change that.
sentences.zh: 我们试图改变这一现状。

sentences.en: The TypeScript team can move quite fast on many things, but for some features they may spend years intentionally exploring options and making prototypes before picking the right implementation.
sentences.zh: TypeScript团队可以在许多事情上快速行动，但对于某些功能，他们可能会花费数年时间有意探索选项并制作原型，然后再选择正确的实现。

sentences.en: A Rust port has to follow those decisions closely, or it will eventually fall apart and become incompatible.
sentences.zh: Rust端口必须密切关注这些决策，否则它最终会崩溃并变得不兼容。

sentences.en: We have to preserve the TypeScript language strictly based on its original implementation – and the TypeScript team should remain solely responsible for deciding what that looks like.
sentences.zh: 我们必须严格基于其原始实现来保留TypeScript语言， TypeScript团队应全权负责确定其外观。

items.title: Cutting our inference bill by 68% by being obsessive about optimization

sentences.en: Cutting our inference bill by 68% by being obsessive about optimization.
sentences.zh: 通过痴迷于优化，将我们的推理账单减少了68%。

sentences.en: When we previously blogged about our AI code reviewer in April , an average review cost a palatable $1.19.
sentences.zh: 当我们之前在4月份发布关于我们的人工智能代码审核器的博客时，平均审核成本为1.19 $。

sentences.en: By the end of August, that figure had shot up to about $2.46.
sentences.zh: 截至8月底，这一数字已飙升至约2.46 $。

sentences.en: We hadn't made any significant architectural changes: the coordinator was still handing work to the same set of specialist reviewers, and the same risk tiers decided how intensive of a review we gave.
sentences.zh: 我们没有进行任何重大的架构更改：协调员仍在将工作交给相同的专业审核员，相同的风险等级决定了我们进行审核的密集程度。

sentences.en: Around mid-September we tasked our agents with working out where those tokens were going and cutting them — aggressively.
With code quality at high effort, the average review now costs just $0.77, down 68% from the $2.43 it averaged over our two most expensive weeks before we started.
Our main goal was to cut costs, but as part of this work we also managed to optimize the reviewer, so that the median review now takes just 1m 32s instead of the 4m 09s it took before.
About 40% of the savings came from changes and optimizations to the reviewer's code, and the rest from experimenting with which models we use and how much effort they put in.
How a review doubled in cost The chart below shows the cost of an average review on each weekday since March.
It holds the mix of review tiers fixed, so a day with more large reviews doesn't skew the data.
The cost per review steadily rose from $1.22 (March) → $1.44 (June) → $1.74 (July) and finally, to $2.32 (August).
A small part of that is that more reviews landed in the most expensive tier (59% of reviews in March and then 65% in August).

items.title: Introducing Clairic, a new System One class of extraction models

sentences.en: Introducing Clairic, a new System One class of extraction models.
Today, we're announcing a preview of a new class of System One-style models: extraction models.
Our first one, Clairic, is available hosted on Workers AI as @cf/cloudflare/clairic.
We intend to release the model open-weights soon.

Clairic is an extraction model that is able to extract, compute, estimate, and forecast values from unstructured inputs — all at a significantly higher accuracy, faster latency, and cheaper cost than traditional LLMs.
Context When System One models were announced by TypeSafe a month ago, it took the industry by storm.

As referenced by TypeSafe in their blog and defined by Daniel Kahneman’s book Thinking, Fast and Slow , a System One model should be fast and precise, which contrasts a System Two model that is capable of deliberate reasoning (like LLMs).
With this, TypeSafe introduced Jev — a model that is purpose-fit for a specific use case, and priced accessibly given its niche domain.
It excelled where LLMs failed, helping users make decisions based on probabilities and well-typed outputs.
The introduction of Jev prompted people to start thinking about a new class of models that were not LLMs and how to integrate them into their workflows.
We were inspired by the concept of System One models and started thinking about other tasks where LLMs are inefficient.
There are many structured-output calls going to frontier LLMs today with the same shapes again and again: What's the invoice total?
